title: Characterizing Stereotypical Bias from Privacy-preserving Pre-Training
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the model's preference for stereotypical associations related to religion. This was evaluated using fill-mask tasks (intrasentence), next-sentence prediction tasks (intersentence), and pseudo-likelihood scoring of sentence pairs embodying stereotypes versus non-stereotypes.
findings: Stereotypical bias related to religion showed a different trend compared to other social categories. While the general trend was a decrease in bias with tighter privacy settings, bias related to religion was found to be 'constant'. In the StereoSet intrasentence task, bias related to religion actually increased as privacy was tightened, while in the CrowS-Pairs benchmark, it remained high and relatively stable.
